editors.name: Prof. Pratima Panigrahi
editors.bio: After earning a Ph.D. in Mathematics from the Indian Statistical Institute, Pratima Panigrahi has been a Professor in the Department of Mathematics at IIT Kharagpur. She has played active editorial and organisational roles in the community, organising national workshops and serving as a regular reviewer for many leading journals. Deeply engaged with national and regional mathematical activity, she has delivered numerous invited lectures and keynotes (both in India and abroad), held important institute responsibilities, and remains committed to outreach through webinars and popular lectures that brings mathematics to wider student audiences.

editors.name: Dr. Himalaya Senapati
editors.bio: After a PhD in Physics, Himalaya has been working in the finance industry, initially as a Core Quant Strat at Goldman Sachs and now as an Equity Derivative Analyst at HSBC. He has also been actively involved as a teacher in various mathematics camps for school students. In his school days, Himalaya consistently ranked among the top 30 students in the country in the mathematics and astronomy olympiads. Additionally, in class IX, he was in the top 6 and represented India in the International Astronomy Olympiad and achieved a silver medal.

editors.name: Dr. Shyam Sundar Agrawal
editors.bio: After completing his PhD in the intersection of Mathematics, Computer Science and Management Science, Shyam followed his passion for teaching and began working with high school students. He brings over twenty-six years of experience in teaching and research. An active contributor to the mathematical community and the Olympiad ecosystem, he has been recognized with multiple state- and national-level awards in Mathematics.

editors.name: Prof. Srinivas K
editors.bio: Srinivas is a Visiting Professor at IISER Tirupati and former Professor H at IMSc, Chennai. A distinguished researcher, he has collaborated widely with institutions across India, Europe, and Canada. He has served on the Executive Council of the Ramanujan Mathematical Society and on the Boards of Studies of several institutions, including NIT Rourkela and the Central University of Tamil Nadu. He was Co-Managing Editor of both the Hardy-Ramanujan Journal and the Journal of the RMS. A key contributor to national training programmes such as MTTS and INSPIRE, he has organized numerous conferences and instructional schools. He remains deeply committed to outreach, delivering many popular talks on Ramanujan’s mathematics, including broadcasts on AIR Delhi.
